Subject: Acme integration — post-call recap & next steps (SDK, auth, routing, prompts)

Thanks again for the call today, Alex — great to meet the SRE and product folks. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Primary use case: in-product contextual assistant (answering product docs + internal KB) and reranking search results with embeddings
- Traffic profile: ~200 reqs/sec peak, 150 tokens avg/generation, strict 100ms p50 latency SLO for short responses
- Security: must run in VPC, keys via customer KMS, SOC2 logs required

Immediate asks / next steps (owners):
1) Tech audit: Dev Patel — sample architecture & SDK auth options (short doc + examples) by EOD Friday
2) Prompt governance: Marissa/Dylan — share recommended system prompt versioning and prompt-injection mitigations + red team offer
3) Procurement: Alex — share procurement timeline + PO contact (cc procurement)

I've attached our integration checklist and a small SDK auth examples snippet to help the SREs review.

A few notes on integration approaches (high level):
- SDK setup: our SDK supports both API-key (hosted) and mTLS/KMS connectors for Private deployments. We can provide a Docker-based starter for on-prem testing.
- Auth/routing: support for route-level policies (latency vs cost) — you can pin production traffic to dedicated pools and fall back to hosted for burst.
- Structured output & tool calling: we recommend explicit JSON-schema outputs + a lightweight verifier on your side to prevent malformed tool calls.
- Embeddings/rerankers: we suggest a two-stage flow: embeddings for nearest-neighbor recall, then a lightweight reranker model for final scoring. We provide trained reranker configs and eval scripts.

If that sounds right, I’ll schedule a short technical follow-up next week with Dev to walk through the SDK examples and auth options. 

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Alex — great questions. Answers below and attached the short SDK snippets (sdk-auth-examples.txt) for the KMS + mTLS case. I'll also drop a quick diagram in Monday's call.

1) mTLS + KMS flow (summary):
- Client obtains short-lived cert via your internal CA (we support cert-based auth to our private control plane).
- Service authenticates with customer KMS to decrypt model encryption keys; rotation is handled via KMS policy and our runtime re-reads keys on rotation window.
- Example flow included in sdk-auth-examples.txt — Dev can walk through code during the follow-up.

2) Routing / fallback:
- Primary: Dedicated pool pinned to your tenant.
- Automatic fallbacks: runtime supports automatic fallback to a compatible hosted model variant when Dedicated capacity isn't available. Policy is configurable (prefer latency vs prefer cost). Fallbacks are executed by the Redwood routing plane — you do not need to change your proxy.

3) Structured output verifier:
- We recommend a synchronous verifier that runs as a small sandboxed process post-generation. It returns either ACCEPT with parsed JSON or REJECT with failure reason.
- On REJECT we suggest graceful degradation: show a condensed fallback to a deterministic template or call the assistant in a higher-precision mode. This avoids 500s while preserving UX.

4) Reranker latency lift:
- Expect ~15–40ms added p90 for a lightweight reranker on top of embedding-based recall (varies by model size and hardware). We can run a small benchmark with your sample data to give a realistic estimate.

Proposed next step: 30-min technical sync Monday 2/16 @ 10:00am PT — Dev to demo SDK mTLS flow and we can walk the verifier approach. Alex / SREs — does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — when you send the prompt governance doc, include:
- System prompt versioning: recommend a semver-like scheme and a changelog per environment (dev/staging/prod)
- Prompt injection mitigations: use a combination of input sanitization, context window limits, and output schema enforcement. Include examples of attack patterns and defensive rewrites.
- Red teaming: offer a scoped red-team engagement (2 weeks) that includes adversarial prompt generation, regression tests tied to eval prompts, and a runbook for rollback.

I'll draft a short one-pager we can share with Alex; Dev, can you add a short line about how the verifier integrates with the runtime (API + error codes)?

Dylan

Alex / team  quick follow-up and attached prompt governance one-pager. Highlights: 
- System prompt versioning: we recommend semantic versions (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) with a changelog per environment. Tag releases to eval suites so regressions are caught before prod promotion.
- Prompt injection mitigations: examples included (escape sequences, instruction sandwiching, context truncation). Recommend both client-side sanitization and server-side policy enforcement.
- Verifier integration: runtime returns explicit error codes (VERIFIER_ACCEPT, VERIFIER_REJECT_SCHEMA, VERIFIER_REJECT_INJECTION) and we expose these via the SDK for routing logic.
- Offer: 2-week red team pilot (adversarial prompt generation + regression creation + eval baselines). Pricing and scope in one-pager.

If you're OK, let's confirm the 30-min sync Monday 2/16 @ 10:00am PT and we can walk the one-pager live.

Thanks,
Marissa
